title: Role of anaerobic bacteria in the metabolic welfare of the colonic mucosa in man
population: Isolated colonocytes from 14 colectomy specimens, 7 of ascending and 7 of descending colon, mostly taken at least 6 cm from a colonic carcinoma
result: With 10 mM n-butyrate as the only substrate, butyrate accounted for 73% of oxygen consumption of colonocytes from the ascending colon and 75% from the descending colon; with 10 mM glucose added, 59% and 72%. Butyrate lowered the share of oxygen consumption attributable to glucose oxidation from 85% to 41% (ascending) and from 30% to 16% (descending). Colonocytes formed ketone bodies, mainly acetoacetate, from butyrate. The author states that the precise contribution of these fatty acids to the colonic mucosa in vivo remains to be shown.
